info.name: Oracle Database Autonomous Recovery Service Database Recovery API
databaseRecovery
Gets a list of all long term backups in a compartment

params.name: compartmentId
params.description: The compartment OCID.

params.name: id
params.description: The long-term backup OCID. Use longTermBackupId to filter a long-term backup based on its unique identifier.

params.name: displayName
params.description: A filter to return only resources that match the entire 'displayname' given.

params.name: protectedDatabaseId
params.description: The protected database OCID. Use protectedDatabaseId to list the long-term backups of a specific protected database.

params.name: lifecycleState
params.description: A filter to return only the resources that match the specified lifecycle state.

params.name: limit
params.description: The maximum number of items to return per page.

params.name: page
params.description: The page token representing the page at which to start retrieving results. This is usually retrieved from a previous list call.

params.name: sortOrder
params.description:
The sort order to use, either ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC).
Allowed values are:
  - ASC
  - DESC

params.name: sortBy
params.description:
The field to sort by. You can provide one sort order (sortOrder). Default order for TIMECREATED is descending. Default order for DISPLAYNAME is ascending. If you do not specify a value, then TIMECREATED is used as the default sort order.
Allowed values are:
  - TIMECREATED
  - DISPLAYNAME

items.docs: Lists the long-term backups associated with a protected database. You can filter the results using the unique identifier (OCID) of a specific compartment, a protected database, or a long-term backup.

info.name: Creates a new long-term backup for the protected database with OCID

items.docs: Creates a long-term backup of a specified protected database.

info.name: Get Long Term Backup

params.name: longTermBackupId
params.description: The long term backup OCID.

items.docs: Retrieves information regarding a long-term backup.

info.name: Update the long term backup identified by the id

params.name: longTermBackupId
params.description: The long term backup OCID.

items.docs: Updates the specified long term backup.

info.name: Delete a LongTermBackup

params.name: longTermBackupId
params.description: The long term backup OCID.

items.docs: Deletes a long-term backup. You can delete a long-term backup only if the current state of the backup is ACTIVE, FAILED, or CANCELED.

info.name: Cancels scheduled long-term backup identified by longTermBackupId

params.name: longTermBackupId
params.description: The long term backup OCID.

items.docs: Cancels a long-term backup that is being created or scheduled to be created. You must specify the unique identifier or OCID of the long-term backup that you want to cancel. You can cancel a long-term backup only if the current state of the backup resource is WAITING_FOR_BACKUP_FROM_DB, or SCHEDULED_FOR_ARCHIVAL, or ARCHIVAL_IN_PROGRESS.

info.name: Delete a provisioned Protected Database

params.name: protectedDatabaseId
params.description: The protected database OCID.

params.name: deletionSchedule
params.description:
Defines a preferred schedule to delete a protected database after you terminate the source database.
* The default schedule is DELETE_AFTER_72_HOURS, so that the delete operation can occur 72 hours (3 days) after the source database is terminated .
* The alternate schedule is DELETE_AFTER_RETENTION_PERIOD. Specify this option if you want to delete a protected database only after the policy-defined backup retention period expires.

items.docs:
Deletes a protected database based on the specified protected database ID.
Only the user or the Oracle Database service that created the protected database is allowed to modify or delete it.

info.name: Cancel the scheduled deletion of the protected database

params.name: protectedDatabaseId
params.description: The protected database OCID.

items.docs: Cancels the scheduled deletion of a protected database, and returns the protected database to an ACTIVE state. You can cancel the deletion only if the protected database is in the DELETE SCHEDULED state.
